title: LVOCheck – Acute diagnostics in patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) for improved triage to thrombectomy treatment (LVOCheck): Subproject evaluating a biomarker-based point-of-care blood test for detection of large vessel occlusion ("LVOCheck-Eva")
summary:
Timely treatment is critical in stroke. Patients with large‑vessel occlusion (LVO) benefit from rapid transport to a thrombectomy‑capable center. LVOCheck‑EVA evaluates a new, affordable point‑of‑care test that measures three blood proteins (NT‑proBNP, D‑Dimer, H‑FABP) directly in the ambulance and combines them with a few clinical details to estimate the probability of an LVO. 

This is a multicenter, prospective observational study conducted in Berlin. Three Mobile Stroke Units will enroll 800 patients with suspected stroke within 24 hours after symptom onset, identified by the emergency dispatch center. 

The primary goal is to determine test accuracy against the final in‑hospital diagnosis (sensitivity and specificity). We will also assess agreement between whole‑blood and plasma measurements, usability and workflow integration, and whether the results can support prehospital triage decisions—such as direct transport to a thrombectomy‑capable center (“targeted mothership”). 

In the long term, a simple rapid test could reduce inter‑hospital transfers, shorten time to treatment, and improve access to specialized care in both urban and rural settings.

interventions.name:
Observational arm (prehospital biomarker POCT on an MSU) for dispatch-identified suspected stroke (symptom onset ≤ 24 h).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Suspected stroke based on the initial dispatch center telephone triage
• Symptom onset or last known well ≤ 24 hours
• Intravenous access established as part of standard care
• Prehospital blood sampling feasible prior to treatment initiation
• Written informed consent from the patient or legal representative (deferred consent if needed)
Exclusion criteria:
• Refusal to participate or withdrawal of written consent (by patient or legal representative)
• Blood sampling not possible for any reason
• Unable to perform a full NIHSS due to clinical status (e.g., coma/intubated)
• Pregnancy
